head: working-tree
subject: HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 field-name/value validation use shared byte tables
change: HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 each carried their own field-name validator: a range check for uppercase plus a switch over lowercase letters, digits and token punctuation, per byte. A new src/http/field_name.zig exposes one shared validator backed by a 256-byte table that already excludes uppercase, and both runtimes use it. The shared src/http/field_value.zig control-byte check also moved from two comparisons per byte to a 256-byte invalid-byte table (0x00-0x1f except tab, and 0x7f). The accepted grammar and error contract are unchanged; the shared module has its own tests for pseudo names, uppercase, control bytes and non-token punctuation.

full_library.note: The first run under a host-load spike reported an unrelated gRPC connect-race failure with the same Huffman error-trace shape seen in earlier loaded-host runs; the immediate rerun with the same binary passed 6777/6777. The total includes the three new shared field-name tests.

notes: The two stages are sequential: the name-table stage compares the tag-based validator with the old per-byte switch, and the value-table stage compares the name-table binary with the added value table. Combined with the earlier pseudo-header tag change, request header validation moved from 167.0 ns/block in the pre-tag binary to 131.5 ns/block after both tables. The non-target HPACK rows in each batch are layout noise; the two roundtrip rows moved by about 1% in opposite directions across the stages. HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 now share one name validator, so the grammar cannot drift between the two runtimes. The http2-hpack baseline was re-recorded with nine entries, including header-validation, under the unpinned cpu32 fingerprint. The host was loaded during the batches (load average roughly 5 to 20), so only interleaved ratios are claimed.
